summary: Agent spawns interactive PTY driven by remote relay WebSocket
details: The package connects to a remote relay WebSocket (default wss://msclaude.ai) and dispatches server-delivered `terminal_input` messages into a locally spawned interactive PTY running the user's shell (`/bin/bash` on POSIX, `powershell.exe` on Windows). In createTerminalManager, `ptyProcess = pty.spawn(shell, [], {...})` is paired with a `write(data)` that pipes untrusted socket frames straight into the PTY; connection.js routes `ws.on('message',...)` frames of type `terminal_input` to that write. Any party who reaches the relay session (session URL / shared password / E2E key) can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host running the agent. The same relay channel also drives `handleTunnelRequest` / `handleTunnelWsOpen`, which issue HTTP requests and open WebSocket connections to `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the host (gated by a user-configurable allowlist in `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json`, disabled by default), and file/git handlers (`handleUpdateFile`, `handleCreateFile`, `handleDeleteFile`, `handleUploadFile`, `handleGitCommit`, `handleGitPush`, `handleGitDiscard`) that read, write, and delete arbitrary files and mutate git repositories on the host. The remote-control surface is the package's advertised purpose ("Claude Code from any browser"), but the trigger is a remote WebSocket message reaching an interactive shell, and blast radius on a compromised or shared relay session is full-host RCE plus arbitrary filesystem and git mutation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
